neighbours.label: A noun naming a lack or open problem (gaps, uncertainties, doubts, delays) as the thing that exists or remains, read at the noun or its verb
fire: Even after the audit, uncertainties remain about where the money went.
The witness told a long story, but it still has gaps that nobody can fill.
Among the engineers, doubts remain over whether the dam will hold.
For most of the season, delays have been the rule rather than the exception.
In the official record, gaps appear wherever the minister was involved.
Despite the new data, uncertainties persist regarding the size of the fish stock.
After two reviews, questions remain about how the contract was awarded.
In the northern districts, shortfalls have been reported every winter.
quiet: Even after the audit, the accountants agree about where the money went.
The witness told a long story, and it is complete in every detail.
Among the engineers, confidence is high that the dam will hold.
For most of the season, trains have been running exactly on time.
In the official record, entries appear wherever the minister was involved.
Thanks to the new data, estimates of the size of the fish stock improved.
After two reviews, everyone understands how the contract was awarded.
In the northern districts, harvests have been larger every summer.

notes: Card top examples are mixed (gaps, Uncertainties, Darkness, a firstPacket=True flag, Japanese が). Probes: 'Uncertainties remain' 0.35, 'Doubts remain' 0.29, 'has gaps' 0.24, 'Delays have been' 0.22; growth sentences 0.01-0.08. It also fired 0.6-0.7 on `isFirst = True` / `firstPacket = True` flags, which this label does not cover. Weak guess.
